description: Canonical Work metadata is authored as YAML 1.2. Work v2 stores active nodes in index.yaml, keeps source provenance inline, and keeps every structured record in YAML, including a collocated disposable UAT accounts.yaml fixture.

ids.description: Unique stable Work IDs used for graph edges.

repository.description: Direct repository name or path; example nivo-backend.

revision.description: Exact inspected or implemented full lowercase Git SHA (40 or 64 hex characters).

path.description: Normalized repository-relative source or evidence path using forward slashes; no absolute paths, traversal, empty segments, backslashes, drive/stream colon or control characters.

lineRange.description: Optional source line span, for example 40-58.

symbol.description: Class, function, route or component name.

sourceRef.description: Direct source observation at an exact repository revision and path; no resource manifest is involved. Each observed structured specification source binds to an entry on its owning node by repository, path and revision.

purpose.description: Why the module exists and the user or business outcome it serves.

included.description: Behaviors and responsibilities inside this module.

excluded.description: Nearby concerns intentionally outside this module.

scope.description: Boundary of the SRS; list what is included and explicitly excluded.

responsibilities.description: What the actor must do in this module.

rights.description: What the actor is allowed to do.

restrictions.description: What the actor must not do or conditions that limit access.

actors.description: People or systems that interact with the module.

behavior.description: Observable behavior the system must provide.

functionalRequirements.description: Required observable module behaviors, one compact title and behavior per item.

subject.description: Business entity or concept whose state is described.

states.description: Allowed business states for the subject.

rules.description: Constraints, transitions or invariants that govern the subject.

dataAndStates.description: Business data subjects, allowed states and transition rules.

preconditions.description: Facts that must hold before the flow starts.

actor.description: Person or system performing this step.

action.description: Action performed during the flow or UAT step.

systemResponse.description: Observable response required from the system.

alternatives.description: Valid alternate paths through the flow.

errors.description: Expected error cases and required handling.

postconditions.description: Facts that must hold after successful completion.

flows.description: End-to-end business journeys with preconditions, steps and outcomes.

quality.description: Quality concern such as security, accessibility or latency.

observableCriterion.description: Measurable or directly observable success condition.

verification.description: How the criterion or implementation change is checked.

nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Quality requirements expressed as observable criteria with a verification method; unknown targets must be stated as unresolved rather than invented.

unresolvedQuestions.description: Unknowns that require a person or source to resolve.

inputsOutputs.description: Business inputs accepted and outputs produced at the module boundary.

inputs.description: Required business information or triggers entering the module.

outputs.description: Observable business results emitted by the module.

aiAuthority.description: Explicit boundary between actions the AI system/service may perform and decisions reserved for a person.

allowed.description: Actions the AI system/service is authorized to perform without impersonating a user.

requiresHumanDecision.description: Business decisions that require an accountable person.

exceptions.description: Exceptional business cases that alter the normal flow; keep exclusions in scope.excluded.

businessSpec.description: Module SRS: business outcome, scope, behavior, rules, quality and acceptance; it defines what is needed.
